Silent
sī´lent
adj. (making no sound; rendering Hebrew damam, Greek sigao)
From Latin silere, to be still. Scripture's silences are weighted — God's, the accused's, and heaven's.

Biblical Definition

Silent means without speech. Hannah's is misread by a priest: she spoke in her heart, only her lips moved, and Eli thought her drunk (1Sa 1:13). Isaiah's Servant is silent under injustice: “he was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he opened not his mouth” (Isa 53:7), and Christ fulfils it before Pilate — “he answered him to never a word; insomuch that the governor marvelled greatly” (Mat 27:14). Habakkuk commands, “the LORD is in his holy temple: let all the earth keep silence before him” (Hab 2:20).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines silent as not speaking; mute; dumb; habitually taciturn; still; having no sound; and not mentioning, saying nothing.

expand to see more

SILENT, a. Not speaking; mute; dumb; habitually taciturn.

2. Having no sound; still; having no noise; as the silent watches of the night.

3. Not operative; wanting efficacy.

4. Not mentioning; not proclaiming.

Key Scripture

Isa 53:7 — "He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he opened not his mouth: he is brought as a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is dumb, so he openeth not his mouth."

Mat 27:14 — "And he answered him to never a word; insomuch that the governor marvelled greatly."

Hab 2:20 — "But the LORD is in his holy temple: let all the earth keep silence before him."

1Sa 1:13 — "Now Hannah, she spake in her heart; only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard: therefore Eli thought she had been drunken."

Modern Corruption

Silence is read as weakness or as having no answer, and the strongest man in the Gospels used it before the one court that could have killed Him.

expand to see more

Matthew 27:14 records the effect rather than the reason: he answered him to never a word; insomuch that the governor marvelled greatly. Christ was not without a defence — He had answered questions all through His ministry and would answer the high priest's direct oath. The silence before Pilate was chosen, and it fulfilled a prophecy written seven hundred years before about a lamb dumb before her shearers. Restraint of that kind requires more strength than any speech.

Habakkuk 2:20 gives the congregation its own use of silence: the LORD is in his holy temple: let all the earth keep silence before him. It stands at the end of a chapter of woes against the proud. Silence here is not emptiness but the appropriate response to a Presence, and a worship service with no room for it has removed the one posture Habakkuk prescribes.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew damam (H1826), to be silent, still; chashah (H2814), to hold peace; Greek sigao (G4601), to keep silence.

expand to see more

Hebrew damam (H1826) — to be silent, still; Psalm 4:4, Habakkuk 2:20, Leviticus 10:3, Aaron held his peace.

Hebrew alam (H481) — to be dumb, silent; Isaiah 53:7, as a sheep before her shearers is dumb.

Greek siopao (G4623) — to be silent; Matthew 26:63, Mark 14:61.

Usage

"“He opened not his mouth” — silence chosen, and prophesied."

"“The governor marvelled greatly” — the effect on a man used to speeches."

"“Let all the earth keep silence before him” — a posture worship needs room for."
